SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL
PPQ & Q-SERIES PISTOLS — 2846985 (US), 05 AUG 19 (2019)
cleanIntro: Walther Arms publishes one US book for the centerfire PPQ, and it is titled for the series rather than the model: 'PPQ & Q-Series Pistols'. Inside, it splits its own family in exactly one place - the magazine release. Classic guns have the ambidextrous paddle behind the trigger guard; the M2 has the reversible thumb button on the frame. Yours is the button gun, and that one difference is the first thing this guide makes you confirm, because half of the book's readers own the other one.

steps.title: Confirm you have the M2 - look at the magazine release
steps.action: Look at where the magazine release sits. On the M2 Models it is a thumb-operated push button on the frame behind the trigger guard and it is reversible for left- or right-hand use. On the Classic Models it is an ambidextrous paddle built into the trigger guard itself. If you have a paddle, this is not the M2 procedure.
steps.prose: This is the only place in forty-four pages where Walther distinguishes the two, and it is a real hardware difference, not a badge. It matters at the bench because the M2's button comes out for reversal with a drift and a small screwdriver, and the Classic paddle does not come out at all - so an instruction written for one is simply wrong for the other.
steps.aside: The parts legend says the same thing in shorthand: item 13, Magazine Release, reads 'a. (M2) reversible' and 'b. (Classic) ambidextrous'.
steps.quote: The slide release and paddle style magazine release (featured on the Classic Models) are ambidextrous and the thumb operated magazine release push button (featured on the M2 Models), conveniently located on the frame, is reversible for either left- or right-hand use.
steps.cite:
SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL
PPQ & Q-SERIES PISTOLS — 2846985 (US), 05 AUG 19 — 3.1 Main Features, printed p.12 (PDF p.12)

steps.title: Striker fired, constant trigger pull - which is why the strip needs a trigger press
steps.action: Understand what you are holding before you strip it: the PPQ and Q-Series are striker fired semi-automatic pistols with a constant trigger pull. There is no hammer to lower and no decocker.
steps.prose: A constant-pull striker gun has no second, lighter shot and no visible cocked indicator on the back of the slide, and that is exactly why Walther's field strip requires the trigger to be pressed. Everything that follows is built around getting to that press with a gun you have proved empty twice.
steps.quote: The PPQ & Q-Series pistols are striker fired semi-automatic pistols with constant trigger pull.
steps.cite:
SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL
PPQ & Q-SERIES PISTOLS — 2846985 (US), 05 AUG 19 — 3.1 Main Features, printed p.12 (PDF p.12)

steps.title: Magazine out first, then rack to clear the chamber
steps.action: Point the pistol in a safe direction with your finger off the trigger and out of the trigger guard. Depress the magazine release and remove the magazine. Then, muzzle safe and finger still off the trigger, grasp the serrated sides of the slide from the rear and briskly draw it fully rearward to extract and clear any cartridge from the chamber.
steps.prose: Magazine first, always, and briskly rather than gently - a slow rack is the classic way to leave a live round balanced on the feed ramp instead of throwing it clear. On an M2 the button is under your firing thumb, so this is a one-handed move if you want it to be.
steps.quote: Point the pistol in a safe direction. Make sure your finger is off the trigger and out of the trigger guard. Depress the magazine release and remove the magazine (5.1.1 Fig. 1).
steps.cite:
SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL
PPQ & Q-SERIES PISTOLS — 2846985 (US), 05 AUG 19 — 5.1.1 Field-Stripping Disassembly, printed p.24 (PDF p.24)

steps.title: Lock it open and look into the chamber AND down the magazine well
steps.action: Pull the slide fully to the rear, press upward on the slide stop lever while letting the slide move slightly forward so it locks open. Look into the chamber and down through the magazine well and verify no ammunition remains.
steps.prose: Two openings, two looks. Walther asks for the magazine well as well as the chamber because a magazine that did not drop free is still a magazine in the gun, and on a striker pistol you are about to press the trigger. Do not rely on the loaded chamber indicator for this - the book says the same in its own warning.
steps.quote: Pull the slide fully to the rear, press upward on the slide stop lever while letting the slide move slightly forward thereby locking the slide open
steps.cite:
SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL
PPQ & Q-SERIES PISTOLS — 2846985 (US), 05 AUG 19 — 5.1.1 Field-Stripping Disassembly, printed p.25 (PDF p.25)
steps.warn: DO NOT RELY UPON THE LOADED CHAMBER INDICATOR TO VERIFY THE PRESENCE OR ABSENCE OF A ROUND IN THE CHAMBER.

steps.title: Close the slide, then press the trigger - this is the step that demands the checks above
steps.action: Pull the slide slightly to the rear and slowly release it forward. Then, with the pistol pointed in a safe direction, squeeze the trigger fully to the rear.
steps.prose: There is no way around this on a PPQ: the striker has to be released before the take down catch will let the slide off. Walther puts a full-width warning here for the obvious reason. If you did not look into the chamber and the magazine well a moment ago, go back and do it now rather than pressing the trigger on trust.
steps.quote: Point the pistol in a safe direction. Squeeze the trigger fully to the rear.
steps.cite:
SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL
PPQ & Q-SERIES PISTOLS — 2846985 (US), 05 AUG 19 — 5.1.1 Field-Stripping Disassembly, printed p.25 (PDF p.25)
steps.warn: TO COMPLETE DISASSEMBLY, YOU WILL BE REQUIRED TO PULL THE TRIGGER.

steps.title: Take down catch down on both sides, slide forward off the frame
steps.action: Grip the take down catch from above on both sides and press downwards, then move the slide forward and remove it from the frame.
steps.prose: Both sides at once, from above - the catch is a two-eared bar and pressing one ear alone cocks it in its slot and it will not release. Fingernails on top of both ears, thumb under the frame, and it drops with very little force. If it fights you, the striker has not been released.
steps.quote: Grip the take down catch from above on both sides and press downwards (5.1.1 Fig. 5).
steps.cite:
SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL
PPQ & Q-SERIES PISTOLS — 2846985 (US), 05 AUG 19 — 5.1.1 Field-Stripping Disassembly, printed p.25 (PDF p.25)

steps.title: Recoil guide rod assembly out from under the barrel
steps.action: Remove the recoil guide rod assembly from below the barrel while compressing the spring.
steps.prose: Compress it slightly first so the polymer end unseats from the barrel lug rather than being levered out of it. It is a captive assembly, so nothing will jump apart, but the spring is stiff and it will skip out of your fingers across the bench if you let it.
steps.quote: Remove the recoil guide rod assembly from below the barrel while compressing the spring (5.1.1 Fig. 6).
steps.cite:
SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL
PPQ & Q-SERIES PISTOLS — 2846985 (US), 05 AUG 19 — 5.1.1 Field-Stripping Disassembly, printed p.25 (PDF p.25)

steps.title: Thread protector if fitted, then the barrel out of the slide
steps.action: If your barrel is threaded, remove the thread protector by turning it counter clockwise. Then remove the barrel from the slide.
steps.prose: The thread protector is only on threaded-barrel guns; if yours has a plain muzzle there is nothing to unscrew. The barrel then lifts out of the slide with a slight tilt - it does not need to be forced through the front.
steps.quote: Remove the thread protector by turning it counter clockwise. (if barrel is threaded)
steps.cite:
SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL
PPQ & Q-SERIES PISTOLS — 2846985 (US), 05 AUG 19 — 5.1.1 Field-Stripping Disassembly, printed p.26 (PDF p.26)

steps.title: Field strip complete - four parts and a magazine
steps.action: Frame, slide, barrel, recoil guide rod assembly and magazine. That is the full field strip. Walther is explicit that you never take a PPQ further than this except for the striker, extractor and magazine work its own manual publishes.
steps.prose: Everything routine is reachable now: the bore from the chamber end, the breech face, the extractor claw, the locking surfaces on the barrel and the frame rails. The deep clean below is the striker, the extractor and the magazine, and it needs a 5/64-inch punch.
steps.quote: Move the slide forward, and remove it from the frame.
steps.cite:
SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL
PPQ & Q-SERIES PISTOLS — 2846985 (US), 05 AUG 19 — 5.1.1 Field-Stripping Disassembly, printed p.25 (PDF p.25)
steps.warn: NEVER DISASSEMBLE YOUR HANDGUN BEYOND THE FIELD STRIPPING PROCESS OUTLINED IN THIS MANUAL.

deepSteps.title: Slide end cap off with a 5/64-inch punch
deepSteps.action: With the pistol field stripped, place the muzzle end of the slide on a smooth flat surface, grasp the rear serrations, push in the pin through the square opening at the top right of the slide end cap with a 5/64" (2 mm) drift punch, and slide the end cap downwards off the slide.
deepSteps.prose: The end cap is under striker-spring pressure the whole time it is in place, which is why one hand holds the slide down on the bench while the other works the punch. Push the pin in, do not try to drive it out - it is a plunger, not a retaining pin, and it only has to move far enough to free the cap.
deepSteps.quote: Place the muzzle end of the slide on a smooth, flat surface. Grasp the slide at the rear slide serrations, push in the pin through the square opening located at the top right side of the slide end cap using a 5/64” (2 mm) drift punch (5.2.1 Fig. 1) and remove the slide end cap by sliding it downwards (5.2.1 Fig. 2).
deepSteps.cite:
SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL
PPQ & Q-SERIES PISTOLS — 2846985 (US), 05 AUG 19 — 5.2.1 Remove Striker Assembly, printed p.27 (PDF p.27)
deepSteps.warn: WEAR SAFETY GLASSES EVERY TIME YOU ASSEMBLE OR DISASSEMBLE YOUR FIREARM.

deepSteps.title: Striker assembly out of the slide
deepSteps.action: Remove the striker assembly from the slide.
deepSteps.prose: It comes out rearward as a single captive unit once the end cap is off. Keep it that way - there is nothing inside it an owner is asked to open, and the channel it came out of is the one part of the pistol Walther tells you never to lubricate.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the striker assembly from the slide (5.2.1 Fig. 3).
deepSteps.cite:
SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL
PPQ & Q-SERIES PISTOLS — 2846985 (US), 05 AUG 19 — 5.2.1 Remove Striker Assembly, printed p.27 (PDF p.27)

deepSteps.title: The striker channel stays DRY
deepSteps.action: Clean the striker channel and the striker assembly dry - a brush and a dry patch, nothing more. Do not lubricate inside the striker assembly.
deepSteps.prose: This is the single most commonly ignored instruction in any striker pistol manual and it has an actual failure mode attached: oil in the channel collects unburned powder and carbon into a paste that slows the striker, and a slow striker gives light primer strikes. The channel is designed to let the striker run free, not lubricated.
deepSteps.quote: Do not lubricate inside the striker assembly, this creates the potential for residue build up
deepSteps.cite:
SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL
PPQ & Q-SERIES PISTOLS — 2846985 (US), 05 AUG 19 — 5.6 Lubrication, caution, printed p.32 (PDF p.32)

deepSteps.title: Magazine floorplate off with a 5/32-inch punch
deepSteps.action: Using a 5/32" (4 mm) punch, depress the floorplate catch through the hole in the floorplate, then slide the floorplate forward off the magazine tube while continuing to hold the catch down. Remove the catch and spring through the bottom of the tube, then turn the tube right side up and remove the follower.
deepSteps.prose: Hold a thumb over the floorplate as it slides - the magazine spring is compressed the whole length of the tube and the catch is the only thing holding it. A +2 magazine is different: it has a metal tab at the rear base that has to be pushed up with a flat screwdriver before the floorplate will move.
deepSteps.quote: Using a 5/32” (4 mm) punch, depress the floorplate catch through the hole in the floorplate (5.4.1 Fig. 1).
deepSteps.cite:
SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL
PPQ & Q-SERIES PISTOLS — 2846985 (US), 05 AUG 19 — 5.4.1 Magazine Disassembly, printed p.29 (PDF p.29)
deepSteps.warn: THE MAGAZINE SPRING IS UNDER PRESSURE. USE CAUTION WHEN STRIPPING DOWN THE MAGAZINE.

deepSteps.title: Magazines are model-specific - do not mix them across your safe
deepSteps.action: Keep the magazines with the pistol they came from. Walther's caution is that a magazine designed for one model may physically insert into another and still not function properly in it.
deepSteps.prose: A PPQ M2 magazine and a Classic magazine are not the same part despite fitting the same well, and a 9mm and a .40 tube are not interchangeable either. This is worth a minute at the end of a cleaning session: mark them, keep them together, and never let a stranger's magazine into your box.
deepSteps.quote: Do not interchange magazines from one model to another model pistol.
deepSteps.cite:
SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL
PPQ & Q-SERIES PISTOLS — 2846985 (US), 05 AUG 19 — 5.4 Magazine, caution, printed p.29 (PDF p.29)

deepSteps.title: Deep clean complete - the extractor is as far as Walther goes
deepSteps.action: The book publishes one more procedure beyond this - the extractor and striker safety, which need the striker out first and a hand over the plunger so it does not fly. Anything past that is a gunsmith's job with genuine Walther parts.
deepSteps.prose: The extractor work is worth doing only when you have a reason - a stoppage pattern, or grit you can see behind the claw. There is a striker safety plunger and an extractor plunger under there, both sprung, both small, and both easy to lose on a workshop floor.
deepSteps.quote: WEAR SAFETY GLASSES, AND WHILE YOU REMOVE THE EXTRACTOR, BE SURE TO CONTROL THE STRIKER SAFETY AND
deepSteps.cite:
SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL
PPQ & Q-SERIES PISTOLS — 2846985 (US), 05 AUG 19 — 5.3.1 Remove Extractor, warning, printed p.27 (PDF p.27)

cleaning.name: BARREL & BREECH
tasks: From the chamber end, push a brush through the bore until the bristles fully exit at the muzzle, then pull it back until they fully exit at the chamber end
Use a powder-removing solvent and a brass bristle bore brush to take lead and firing residue out of the barrel
With a small brush dipped in solvent, clear deposits from around the breech face, the chamber end of the barrel, the extractor and the adjacent areas
Clean the barrel ramp where the locking block cams the barrel - that surface carries the load every shot

cleaning.name: SLIDE, FRAME & STRIKER CHANNEL
tasks: Remove residue on the frame with light brushing and a solvent
Wipe the slide rails and the frame guides dry before any oil goes near them
Clean the striker channel DRY - no solvent left standing in it and no oil in it at all
Avoid prolonged solvent immersion and prolonged ultrasonic cleaning; never use ammonia-based or strong alkaline solvents on a Walther

cleaning.name: LUBRICATION & MAGAZINE
tasks: A light film of high quality gun lubricant on all external metal surfaces, then wipe clean
One drop of lubricant on the slide guides and one on the trigger bar - one drop, not a bead
One drop on the safety plunger and the disconnector cut in the slide
A light film on the magazine's external metal surfaces; keep oil out of the inside of the tube
In a cold climate, use a lubricant that will not congeal at low temperatures

reassembly: Hold the slide upside down and place the barrel inside it with the locking lugs oriented as the book shows.
Refit the thread protector if your barrel is threaded.

Insert the recoil guide rod assembly: small end of the rod into the spring mounting at the front of the slide, large polymer end into the lower barrel recess, compressing the spring as it goes. It is normal for the assembly to flex.

Grasp the slide by the rear serrations as far back as possible and push it from the front into the slide guides of the frame, far enough for the take down catch to engage and with the rear slide guides engaged too.
Release the slide and let it run fully forward into the locked position.
fncheck: With the magazine out and the chamber confirmed empty: the slide should run its full stroke and go into battery under its own spring; the slide stop should lock it open off an empty magazine and release it cleanly; the take down catch must sit fully up and flush on both sides; the trigger should have its constant pull with a positive reset you can feel and hear; and the M2's push-button magazine release should drop an empty magazine free without help. Look at the extractor from the right side with a dummy round chambered to confirm the loaded chamber indicator still shows red - but never rely on it in place of looking into the chamber.
